en: How was your journey last night?
tamil: நேத்து ராத்திரி பயணம் எப்படி இருந்துச்சு?
context: Asking a relative who just arrived.
explain: 'How was...?' asks for an opinion about a past event.
usage: Use it to be polite to guests who travelled a long way.
leelaQ: How was your last long journey?
answer: It was tiring, but the train was on time.

en: I have already finished my report, so I can go home.
tamil: என் ரிப்போர்ட்டை ஏற்கனவே முடிச்சுட்டேன், அதனால நான் வீட்டுக்கு போகலாம்.
context: Telling your team leader you are done.
explain: 'Already' with present perfect shows the work is done earlier than expected.
usage: Use it with a team leader to say your work is completed.
leelaQ: Have you finished all your work for today?
answer: Yes, I have finished everything and I am free now.

en: Can you explain what happened in the meeting yesterday?
tamil: நேத்து மீட்டிங்ல என்ன நடந்துச்சுன்னு விளக்க முடியுமா?
context: Asking a colleague who attended the meeting.
explain: 'Can you explain' is a friendly request. The next part is in normal statement order.
usage: Use it with a colleague when you missed a meeting.
leelaQ: What did you discuss in your last meeting?
answer: We discussed the plan for next month.

en: The funniest thing happened today; the teacher called me by my father's name.
tamil: இன்னைக்கு ஒரு காமெடி நடந்துச்சு, டீச்சர் என்னை எங்கப்பா பேர் சொல்லி கூப்பிட்டாங்க.
context: Telling a friend a funny incident from school or college.
explain: The semicolon joins two related ideas. 'Funniest' is the superlative of 'funny'.
usage: Use it to start a funny story with friends.
leelaQ: What is the funniest thing that happened to you recently?
answer: My friend sat on my chair and fell down laughing.

en: I could not find my keys anywhere this morning.
tamil: இன்னைக்கு காலையில என் சாவியை எங்கயும் காணல.
context: Explaining why you were late.
explain: 'Could not' is the negative past of 'can'. It shows you were not able to do it.
usage: Use it to explain a delay caused by a lost item.
leelaQ: Where do you usually keep your keys?
answer: I keep them on a hook near the door.

en: Early in the morning, we reached Chennai and took a cab to the hotel.
tamil: அதிகாலையில சென்னை போய் சேர்ந்து, கேப் புடிச்சு ஹோட்டலுக்கு போனோம்.
context: Describing the start of a trip.
explain: Time phrases like 'early in the morning' set the scene at the start of a story.
usage: Use it to describe how a journey began.
leelaQ: How did you reach your last holiday place?
answer: We went by train and then took a taxi to the resort.

en: Why were you late to the office yesterday?
tamil: நேத்து ஏன் ஆபீசுக்கு லேட்டா வந்தீங்க?
context: A manager politely asking about a delay.
explain: 'Were' is the past of 'are' for 'you'. 'Why' asks for the reason.
usage: Use it with a team member who came late and needs to explain.
leelaQ: Why were you late the last time?
answer: I was late because of heavy traffic.

en: I slipped on the wet floor, but luckily nobody saw me.
tamil: ஈரத்தரையில வழுக்கி விழுந்துட்டேன், நல்ல வேளையா யாரும் பார்க்கல.
context: Telling a friend about an embarrassing moment.
explain: 'But' shows a good point after a bad event. 'Luckily' adds a positive feeling.
usage: Use it to share an embarrassing but harmless story.
leelaQ: Have you ever felt embarrassed in public?
answer: Yes, I once walked into a glass door in a mall.

en: Have you finished your lunch yet?
tamil: நீங்க இன்னும் லஞ்ச் முடிக்கலையா?
context: Asking a colleague before a meeting.
explain: 'Yet' is used in questions and negatives with present perfect.
usage: Use it to check if someone is free for a meeting.
leelaQ: Have you eaten lunch yet today?
answer: Yes, I have eaten a full meal.

en: Our team has worked on this project since January.
tamil: எங்க டீம் ஜனவரில இருந்து இந்த ப்ராஜெக்ட்ல வேலை செய்யுது.
context: Telling a client how long the project has been going.
explain: 'Since' is used with a starting point in time, like January or Monday.
usage: Use it in meetings to show how long you have been doing something.
leelaQ: Which project have you been working on for a long time?
answer: I have been working on a billing project since March.

en: Please tell us a story from your childhood.
tamil: உங்க சின்ன வயசு கதை ஒண்ணு சொல்லுங்க.
context: Asking a grandparent or elder.
explain: 'Please' makes it polite. 'From your childhood' says what kind of story.
usage: Use it with elders who enjoy sharing old memories.
leelaQ: Which childhood story do you remember the most?
answer: I remember a story about a clever crow.

en: Last Sunday we cleaned the whole house before the guests came.
tamil: போன ஞாயித்துக்கிழமை விருந்தாளிங்க வர்றதுக்கு முன்னாடி வீடு முழுக்க சுத்தம் பண்ணோம்.
context: Telling a friend how you prepared for guests.
explain: 'Before' joins two past events. The cleaning happened first.
usage: Use it to talk about family chores and preparations.
leelaQ: What did you do last Sunday at home?
answer: I helped my mother clean the kitchen and then we watched TV.

en: The bus did not come on time, so I took an auto.
tamil: பஸ் நேரத்துக்கு வரல, அதனால ஆட்டோ புடிச்சேன்.
context: Explaining a change of plan.
explain: 'Did not come' is negative past. 'So' shows the result.
usage: Use it to explain a small delay to a manager or a friend.
leelaQ: What do you do when the bus does not come?
answer: I take an auto or ask a friend for a lift.

en: I took the wrong train and ended up in a different town.
tamil: தப்பான ரயில்ல ஏறி வேற ஊருக்கு போயிட்டேன்.
context: Telling a friend about a travel mistake.
explain: 'Ended up' means a surprising result at the end of a series of events.
usage: Use it to tell a funny travel mistake story.
leelaQ: Have you ever made a mistake while travelling?
answer: Yes, I once got into the wrong bus and reached another area.

en: What was your favourite game as a child?
tamil: சின்ன வயசுல உங்களுக்கு புடிச்ச விளையாட்டு என்ன?
context: Asking a friend about childhood.
explain: 'Was' is used with 'your favourite game'. 'As a child' talks about the past.
usage: Use it to know more about a new friend or relative.
leelaQ: Which games did you play with friends in childhood?
answer: I loved playing kabaddi with my neighbours.

en: As a child, I was afraid of dogs.
tamil: சின்ன வயசுல எனக்கு நாய்னா பயம்.
context: Talking about your childhood fears.
explain: 'Was afraid of' describes a feeling in the past. Use 'of' after 'afraid'.
usage: Use it to talk about childhood feelings with friends.
leelaQ: What were you afraid of as a child?
answer: I was afraid of the dark and slept with the light on.

en: Did you see the match on TV last night?
tamil: நேத்து ராத்திரி டிவில மேட்ச் பார்த்தீங்களா?
context: Starting a chat with a friend about cricket.
explain: 'Did you watch' is a simple past question. Add a time like 'last night'.
usage: Use it as a friendly opener the day after a big match.
leelaQ: Which match did you enjoy watching the most?
answer: I enjoyed the World Cup final the most.

en: She has already told me the whole story twice.
tamil: அவ முழு கதையையும் எனக்கு ஏற்கனவே ரெண்டு தடவை சொல்லிட்டா.
context: Politely saying a friend repeats the same story.
explain: 'Twice' shows how many times. Present perfect is used when the time is not important.
usage: Use it gently when someone repeats a story you know.
leelaQ: Do you have a friend who tells the same story again and again?
answer: Yes, my uncle tells the same cricket story every time.

en: Could you repeat what you said about the accident?
tamil: விபத்தை பத்தி நீங்க சொன்னதை திரும்ப சொல்ல முடியுமா?
context: Politely asking someone to repeat important news.
explain: 'What you said' is a noun clause. It is in normal statement order.
usage: Use it when you did not hear a part of a serious story.
leelaQ: What do you say when you didn't hear someone clearly?
answer: I say, sorry, could you repeat that please?

en: Then the lights went off, and the whole street became dark.
tamil: அப்புறம் லைட் போயிடுச்சு, தெரு முழுக்க இருட்டாயிடுச்சு.
context: Telling a story about a power cut.
explain: 'Then' moves the story to the next event. 'Went off' means stopped working.
usage: Use it to tell a story step by step in an exciting way.
leelaQ: What happened at your home during the last power cut?
answer: We lit candles and talked for an hour.

en: I haven't eaten anything since morning.
tamil: காலையில இருந்து நான் எதுவும் சாப்பிடல.
context: Telling a friend you are very hungry.
explain: 'Haven't eaten' is present perfect negative. 'Since morning' shows the starting time.
usage: Use it with family or friends when you are hungry after a long day.
leelaQ: What do you do when you are very hungry?
answer: I eat something quickly, like biscuits or fruit.

en: We stayed at my uncle's place for two days during the holidays.
tamil: விடுமுறையில ரெண்டு நாள் மாமா வீட்டுல தங்கினோம்.
context: Telling a colleague about your holiday.
explain: 'For two days' shows how long an action lasted in the past.
usage: Use it to say how long you stayed somewhere.
leelaQ: Where did you stay during your last holiday?
answer: We stayed in a small lodge near the beach.

en: How long were you waiting at the bus stop yesterday?
tamil: நேத்து பஸ் ஸ்டாப்ல நீங்க எவ்வளவு நேரம் காத்திருந்தீங்க?
context: Asking a friend about a long wait yesterday.
explain: 'How long were you waiting' asks about the length of a past wait.
usage: Use it when a friend was late because of a bus delay.
leelaQ: What do you usually do when you have to wait for a long time?
answer: I listen to songs or talk to people near me.

en: I forgot my lunch box at home, so I bought biryani outside.
tamil: லஞ்ச் பாக்ஸை வீட்டுலயே மறந்துட்டேன், அதனால வெளியில பிரியாணி வாங்கினேன்.
context: Telling a colleague why you ate outside.
explain: 'Forgot' and 'bought' are irregular past forms. 'So' gives the result.
usage: Use it to explain a small change in your plan at work.
leelaQ: What did you have for lunch yesterday?
answer: I had curd rice and potato fry.

en: When did you first come to Chennai?
tamil: நீங்க முதல் தடவை எப்ப சென்னைக்கு வந்தீங்க?
context: Asking a colleague about their background.
explain: 'When did you' asks about a past time. Use the base verb 'come' after 'did'.
usage: Use it to know how long a person has lived in a city.
leelaQ: When did you first come to your current city?
answer: I first came here five years ago for work.
